build: PAL, two-sided G64 pair supplied by the contributor (side 1 SHA-256 45e07b32..., side 2 7a402586...); EA loader, no crack or trainer

exclude: stale bytes between the loader and the event manager, unchanged since the title; nothing refers to them
6 parts: Downhill Jam, Downhill Race, Freestyle ramp and others
elsewhere: 6 parts: Downhill Jam, Downhill Race, Freestyle ramp and others

comments.text: RESIDENT LOADER, load entry (JMP $F236). Call with A = file number ($00-$30, file_table $F2F9) and X/Y = load address (lo/hi). Returns carry clear and X/Y = the end address (one past the last byte), or carry set on a drive error. High Jump calls it at $0806 (stub), $08F8, $094E, $0959 and $123F (JMP); it chains files by passing the end of one as the start of the next ($0951). Uses zero page $90-$95 and $E0-$FB
Second loader entry (JMP $F26A): write a file's sectors to disk, same A and X/Y as load_file. Nothing in this snapshot calls it

load_file proper: load_setup (also sends the disk ID), then per sector: end pointer to $F1/$F2 (set_end_ptr), destination page to $EF/$F0 (set_dest_ptr), read_sector_cmd with track $94 and sector $95, wait_transfer for the 256 bytes, next_sector; the page $91 goes up by one each time until $90/$91 reaches the end $92/$93. Only the bytes before the end are stored (the drive still sends whole sectors)
save_file proper: the same sector walk as load_file_body, but each sector goes out through write_sector ($F43A) from the pages at X/Y. No caller in this snapshot

Set up a file transfer: $90/$91 = X/Y (start), $92/$93 = start + length from file_table, $94 = start track, $95 = start sector (made physical by logical_to_physical when the track's interleave is 11). Then sends drive command $0B with $45 $41 (set_disk_id_cmd), which tells the drive to expect disk ID "EA"; a disk with another ID fails its reads

Advance $94/$95 to the next sector of a file: sector = (sector + track_interleave[track]) mod sectors_per_track[track]; when that comes back to 0 every sector of the track has been used and the walk moves to the next track at sector 0, stepping over track 18 (the directory track)
A = file_table start index; returns A = index*11 mod the sector count of track Y, the physical sector that is the index-th in the interleave-11 sequence (0, 11, 1, 12, ... on a 21-sector track)

Resident loader file table, 4 bytes per file, files $00-$30 (49 entries): +0 start track, +1 start sector as an index into that track's interleave sequence (converted to a physical sector at $F2E4), +2/+3 length in bytes (lo/hi). Files $00-$1A are on side 1, $1B-$30 on side 2 (both start again at track 3). Read by load_setup ($F295). Checked: files $0B, $0C, $0E, $0F, $11 and $12 read from side1.g64 with this table equal the snapshot, apart from the bytes of $0B the game writes at run time
file_table +1 column: start sector index of each file (the auto symbol of the indexed read at $F2B4)
file_table +2 column: file length low byte, added to the load address X to make the end pointer $92 ($F29C)

file_table rows from +3 of file $00 to file $0F: length high byte added to Y for $93 ($F2A3). Notable rows: file $0B (track 12) is the resident event manager loaded at $F730; file $0C (track 18 sector 18, 3 bytes) is the disk-side ID; file $0E (track 14, $34FF bytes) is High Jump's first part at $0880; file $0F (track 17, $200 bytes) the font High Jump loads to $6800

file_table rows for files $10-$1F: $10 (track 17, $17D9 bytes, loaded by High Jump to $4000), $11 (track 19, $1284 bytes, to $7000), $12 (track 20, $402C bytes, loaded straight after $11, ending at $C2B0); $13-$1A are other side-1 files; $1B (side 2, track 3, $3780 bytes) is the file event 3 (DOWNHILL) loads
file_table rows for files $20-$2F, all on side 2 ($28, track 14, $378D bytes, is the file event 4 (JAM) loads)
file_table row for file $30 (side 2, track 25 index 14, $09A2 bytes), the last entry; the sectors-per-track table follows
Sectors per track, indexed by track 0-35 (entry 0 unused): 21 for tracks 1-17, 19 for 18-24, 18 for 25-30, 17 for 31-35. Read by next_sector ($F2CE) and logical_to_physical ($F2ED)

Sector step per track, indexed by track 0-35: 1 on tracks 1-3, 18 and 35, 11 on all others. next_sector adds it modulo the track's sector count; load_setup multiplies the start index by 11 when it is 11 or more ($F2B2)

Loader transfer state: 0 = idle or finished, $80 = failed (set with carry at $F648), any other value = a sector transfer is pending (set at $F54A to the destination page high nibble, or $10; only zero, negative and positive are ever tested). Written $F4C2/$F54A/$F4AB/$F650, read by wait_transfer ($F553) and bg_receive ($F57E)
Bytes per call for bg_receive ($F57E) plus one: $14, copied to the countdown $F9 there. Read only at $F58A
Status byte returned by drive command $0C, stored by drive_query_status ($F4A5); nothing in this snapshot reads it
Three bytes ($C0 $F3 $CF) that nothing in this snapshot reads by name; reachable only by an out-of-range track index into track_interleave
Store X/Y as the receive pointer $EF/$F0 (absolute addressing of zero page) for the next transfer
Store X/Y as the end pointer $F1/$F2: receive_bytes stops storing when $EF/$F0 reaches it
Send command $80 (bit 7 set): the drive code takes any such command as JMP ($FFFC), a reset of the drive back to its own DOS. No caller in this snapshot

Ask the drive for one sector: command 1 with track Y and sector X, raw mode ($E8=1: every byte stored, no link bytes followed), clears the byte count $F7 and the end flag $E0. Through send_drive_command

Write one sector: command 5 (on the drive, resets its buffer index), 128 commands 3 each carrying two bytes read from ($EF/$F0), then command 4 with track Y and sector X (patched into $F47C/$F477), which writes the drive's buffer to disk, then wait for the drive's one-byte reply. Called only by save_file_body ($F27F), reached through save_file ($F233), which the shop's save_records ($0BBA) calls; nothing in this snapshot calls save_file
Operand of an LDA # in write_sector: the sector for the final command 4, patched from X at $F43A
Operand of the second LDA #: the track for command 4, patched from Y at $F43D
Send command $0B with track byte Y and sector byte X; the drive code stores them as the expected disk ID (drive zero page $12/$13). load_setup sends $45 $41, "EA"
Send command $0C and receive the one byte it answers (the drive's last job status) into drive_status_byte $F407. No caller in this snapshot
Mark a reply pending (xfer_state = $10) and fall into wait_transfer
Operand of the LDX # at $F4B2: send_drive_command's caller X, patched at $F4B7 and handed back on both exits ($0B here: the sector of the last read)
Operand of the LDY # at $F4B4: the caller's Y, patched at $F4BA ($18 here: track 24, the last read's track)

Send the 3-byte command in $E5 (command), $E6 (track byte), $E7 (sector byte) to the drive code on the serial bus, keeping X/Y (saved into $F4B3/$F4B5, returned by the exit at $F4B2, entered at $F4B1 with carry set on failure). It raises CIA 2 port A bit 3 ($DD00), fails with carry set if bit 7 is already high or bit 6 does not go low then high within 255 polls, drops bit 3, then clocks out 24 bits most significant first: each bit on $DD00 bit 4, strobed by pulsing bit 5. For commands below 3 it marks a reply pending in xfer_state ($F54A). Returns carry clear when the command was taken
wait_transfer's saved Y (written $F55B, restored $F579)
wait_transfer's saved X (written $F55E, restored $F576)

Wait until a pending reply has been received: if xfer_state is non-zero and positive, call receive_bytes until it is 0 (done) or $80 (failed, carry set). Sets the busy flag $F8 so that bg_receive does not run meanwhile; keeps X/Y ($F551/$F552)

Background receive: if no wait_transfer is running ($F8 = 0) and a reply is pending, take up to 19 bytes (count from bg_slice_bytes) and return, so a load can be spread over interrupts. No caller in this snapshot

Receive reply bytes from the drive while the countdown $F9 lasts: for each byte wait (up to $30 polls, else return) for $DD00 bit 7 to go high, then take 8 bits, each read as bit 6 of $DD00 inverted and acknowledged by a pulse on bit 5; bit 7 falling mid-byte means failure (xfer_state = $80). For command 3 and up the single byte is the whole reply. For a sector, raw mode stores each byte at ($EF/$F0) until the end pointer (end flag $E0); the other mode (not used by load_file) takes bytes 0/1 as the next track/sector link and asks for that sector itself ($F63F). After 256 bytes the transfer is done
Loop back to receive_bytes for the next byte of the sector (reached from $F62B while the in-sector count $E1 has not wrapped)
After an event: sort the skaters by score (sort_by_score), then award_place_points for places 0, 1 and 2. Called by show_results ($FB39)

Bubble sort of the skaters by their 24-bit event score, highest first, over num_skaters entries; skipped in practice (practice_flag) or with fewer than 2 skaters. order_pair does each compare and swap
Compare skater $19's 3-byte score in event_scores with skater $19+1's; if it is lower, swap the two skaters' name (16 bytes), score (3), skater_attr, overall_points and skater_ids entries
A = place 0-2: if there is a skater in that place and its score is non-zero, add place_points[place] (5, 3, 1) to its overall_points in decimal mode
Points for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place in an event: 5, 3, 1 (BCD), added to the skater's overall points by award_place_points ($F7F7)

Digit characters '0'-'9','A'-'F' as screen codes for the lower-case character set ($30-$39, $41-$46): print_bcd_byte ($FAD5/$FAE0) indexes it by nibble, and the INSERT SIDE prompt takes the side digit from it ($FA8F)

16-bit shift-register state of random_step ($F90F): low byte $F817, high byte $F818. File $0B sets $01,$08. Nothing in this snapshot calls random_step; the town, entry and play snapshots each hold a different value (entry $0843 is two steps of the generator after play's $1021), so earlier loads step it
High byte of random_state ($08 in file $0B; ROL'd at $F918 and XORed into the result at $F921)
"LESTER  " + 0: the computer opponent's name. Practice and an odd skater out in a two-skater event point the second skater slot ($FE09) here ($FA49, $FF7E)
"PRACTICE" + 0. In practice the first skater slot $FE00 points here ($FA18), so High Jump prints it as the skater's name; also the first word of the PRACTICE AGAIN? menu ($FE30)
"AGAIN?", the rest of the practice menu line, copied with str_practice by the loop at $FE2E (15 bytes, the zero left as a blank)
"YES  NO", the practice menu's choices, copied to screen $05C8 at $FE3D; the cursor arrow goes at $05F1 or $05F5
"NEXT SKATER", shown at screen $059E between turns in a competition ($FF8F)
"SKATING TO ", the loading screen's first words, copied to screen $0599 by show_skating_to ($FAF0)
"SCORES" + 0 + "FOR" + 0, the results header; show_results copies 22 bytes from here, through dest_name, to screen $0458 skipping the zeros ($FB51)

11-character name of the place being loaded, filled from the event name table at $F9DC or with str_skate_shop at $FC76; printed after SKATING TO and in the results header. File $0B holds SKATE SHOP; this snapshot holds HIGH JUMP
"SKATE SHOP ", copied into dest_name by goto_shop ($FC76)
"OVERALL", the column heading for overall points, printed at screen $046F only in a full competition (comp_flag $F89F set, $FB66)
"INSERT SIDE ", copied to screen $0594 by side_check ($FA83); the side digit goes at $05A0
"AND PRESS BUTTON.", copied to screen $05A2 by side_check ($FA97); the prompt then waits for fire on either port

Current event, 0-5 in the order of the tables at $F8A0 (1 RAMP, 2 HIGH JUMP, 3 DOWNHILL, 4 JAM, 5 POOL JOUST; 2 here). 4 and 5 are run two skaters at a time, 5 as a knockout; 2 gets the feet-and-inches results column. Advanced at $FC0B in a competition
Copy of cur_event made when an event's results are shown ($FB3F); archive_event ($FFBF) uses it
PRACTICE AGAIN? choice: 0 = YES, 1 = NO, toggled at $FE8C
Joystick auto-repeat countdown for the practice menu, reset to 8 ($FE79)
Number of skaters entered (0 here, in practice). Bounds the sort, the results list and the turn list ($F748, $FBE7, $FA05)
Index into turn_order of the skater whose turn it is, cleared at $F9FF, advanced at $FF42 and $FF5E
Offset of the next score record in event_scores (3 per skater, 6 per pair in events 4 and 5), advanced at $FF28
Two bytes ($80, $08) that file $0B sets and nothing in this snapshot references
Where the next load goes: 0 = skate shop, 1-5 = an event (set by goto_event $F9A2, read after the side check at $FA76)
Row of the load tables being set up: 6 while the side ID is loaded, the event's row after (written $F9E4)
Disk side the next load needs (1 or 2), from side_table ($F99F); compared with the three bytes of file $0C at $FA6E
Full-competition flag: non-zero runs the events one after another and shows overall points; cleared when the player quits to the shop ($FCB9). Nothing in this snapshot sets it
Load-table rows, one byte per destination (0 none, 1 RAMP, 2 HIGH JUMP, 3 DOWNHILL, 4 JAM, 5 POOL JOUST, 6 side check): load address low byte, patched into the stub at $F928
Load address high byte per destination ($08 for the events, $FD for the side check), patched into the stub at $F92A
Entry point low byte per destination, patched into the stub's JMP at $F93F
Entry point high byte per destination: events enter at $0880 (POOL JOUST at $0820), the side check at $FA69. Patched at $F940
File number per destination: $0D RAMP, $0E HIGH JUMP, $1B DOWNHILL, $28 JAM, $14 POOL JOUST, $0C side ID; patched into the stub at $F926
Event name pointer low byte per destination (names at $F8D8-$F904)
Event name pointer high byte per destination
Disk side per destination: shop 1, RAMP 1, HIGH JUMP 1, DOWNHILL 2, JAM 2, POOL JOUST 1, then 0 for row 6
Event names, 11 characters each, copied into dest_name: "RAMP" $F8D8, "HIGH JUMP" $F8E3, "DOWNHILL" $F8EE, "JAM" $F8F9, "POOL JOUST" $F904
Step the 16-bit shift register random_state ($F817/$F818) once and return A = low XOR high. No caller in this snapshot

Template of the 29-byte load stub that run_load_stub ($FA58) copies to $0800 and jumps to: LDA #file ($F926), LDX #lo ($F928), LDY #hi ($F92A), JSR $F230, SEI, $DC02=$FF, $DC03=0, $DC00=$7F, JMP entry ($F93F/$F940). Patched per destination at $F9B5-$F9CD and $FC84-$FC94. Only its last instruction ($F93E) runs here, to re-enter the loaded event; the rest runs as the copy at $0800
Load stub operand: file number for LDA # (patched at $F9CD from file_no_table, $FC94 with 3 for the shop; $0E for High Jump here)
Load stub operand: load address low byte for LDX # (patched $F9B5, $FC84)
Load stub operand: load address high byte for LDY #, followed by JSR $F230 and the CIA 1 set-up: port A all outputs, port B all inputs, $DC00 = $7F (patched $F9BB, $FC8C)

Last instruction of the load stub, JMP to the loaded event's entry ($F93F/$F940 = $0880 for High Jump). Jumped to in place by event_done to play the same event again without loading it: after YES in practice ($FE99) and between skaters ($FFA7). High Jump's $0880 has been turned into NOPs by then, so this lands on its re-entry at $0883
Low byte of reenter_event's JMP target, the loaded file's entry (patched $F9C1, $FC87; $80 here)
High byte of the JMP target (patched $F9C7, $FC8F; $08 here, so the stub enters High Jump at $0880)

Switch the screen to plain text for the manager's screens: VIC bank 0 ($DD00 bits 0-1 = 3), $D018 = $16 (screen $0400, lower-case character set), $D011 = $1B, $D016 = $C8; SEI, sprites off, raster interrupt off and acknowledged

Wait until $D012 changes to a value below $80: about one line when called in the top half of the frame, up to the end of the frame from the bottom half. A short pacing delay for the fire and joystick polls
Clear the text screen $0400-$07FF to spaces with white colour RAM, background $D021 = 6

Go to destination X (0 = skate shop, 1-5 = an event): note its disk side (side_table) and X in goto_target, fill side_id_buf with $FF and set up a load of row 6 (file $0C, 3 bytes to $FDB2, entry side_check $FA69), so the disk side is checked before every load

Patch the load stub for load-table row X (file, load address, entry), copy the 11-character name to dest_name, clear the screen and switch to text. For an event row it also shows SKATING TO, resets the turn state (turn_index, score_offset, turn_order, turn_count) and fills the skater slots: practice gets PRACTICE and LESTER, a competition gets the first skater (and a second for events 4 and 5). Then run_load_stub
Make the second slot the computer: slot_b_is_cpu = $FF, name LESTER ($F819), attribute $0D
Clear the result slots, copy the 29-byte load stub ($F925) to $0800 and jump to it; the stub loads the file over this code's callers and jumps to the entry

Entry of the side-ID load: if the 3 bytes in side_id_buf all equal wanted_side, go on to the real load (setup_load for the event in goto_target, or goto_shop for 0). Otherwise print INSERT SIDE n AND PRESS BUTTON. (n from hex_digit_chars), wait for fire on either port and try again from goto_event. A failed read leaves the $FF bytes, so a wrong or missing disk asks again

Print the BCD byte A as two digits at ($14),y with leading-zero suppression: $1B counts digits shown so far (zero means still suppressing; a zero byte then just skips two columns), $1C forces the next high digit. Digits from hex_digit_chars. Keeps X; advances Y
Clear the screen and print SKATING TO followed by dest_name on row 10 ($0599 and $05A4)
Fill the second skater slot ($FE09-$FE0B) for skater turn_order[turn_index] (Y = 9 into set_slot_fields)
Fill the first skater slot ($FE00-$FE02) for skater turn_order[turn_index]: name pointer $FCDA + 16*id and skater_attr[id]. Returns X = 3*id

Results screen after every skater has had a turn: text screen, rank_and_award, archive_event, then (not in practice) SCORES FOR <event> with each skater's name and score, two lines apart: feet'inches" for High Jump ($FC1D), WIN/LOSS for POOL JOUST ($FC40), six BCD digits otherwise, and OVERALL points in a competition. Waits for fire to be released and then pressed, then goes to the next event (competition) or the shop

Load the skate shop: name SKATE SHOP, show SKATING TO SKATE SHOP and patch the stub for file 3 at $0880, entry $0880; then run_load_stub
In a competition, print the current skater's overall_points at column $1C of the results line
The player abandoned an event (quit_flag): clear quit_flag and comp_flag and go to the shop through goto_event 0
n*3 for n = 0-9: offset of skater n's 3-byte record in event_scores ($FB1B, $FEAF) and of event n+1's three ids in archive_ids ($FFDC)
Offset of each event's 9-byte block in archive_scores, indexed by finished_event: 0, 0, 9, 18, 27, 36, 45 ($FFC6); only events 1-4 are archived
Per-skater byte, 8 entries (7 in each here), copied to slot byte $FE02/$FE0B ($FB15) and kept with the skater by the sort. Its meaning is not established; High Jump copies $FE02 to $2D83 and $2D8B
skater_attr from skater 1 ($FCD3-$FCD9), the neighbour order_pair swaps with ($F7BB)

Skater names, 16 bytes each, 8 skaters ($FCDA-$FD59): skater 0 here. Zero ends a name. show_results adds $40 to each character and takes $40 back off results above $5A ($FB8E), so letters are kept as $01-$1A; High Jump's printer ANDs each byte with $3F ($125E). The slot pointer $FE00 = $FCDA + 16*skater ($FB21). Empty in this snapshot
skater_names from skater 1 ($FCEA) to skater 3; the sort swaps 16-byte records at $FCDA,y and $FCEA,y ($F78A)
skater_names for skaters 4-7 ($FD1A-$FD59)

event_scores +1 (middle byte; feet in High Jump), read as $FD5B,x by show_results ($FBB9, $FC21)
event_scores +2 (high byte; High Jump's raw height), printed first by show_results ($FBB3)

event_scores +4, the next record's middle byte ($FF1F, $F775)
event_scores +5 to the end of the table ($FD71): the next record's high byte ($FF25, $F77B)
Overall points per skater, 8 BCD bytes; award_place_points adds 5/3/1 ($F7FC) and show_results prints them under OVERALL ($FCAB)
overall_points from skater 1 ($FD73), the neighbour the sort swaps with ($F7C8)
Top three scores (9 bytes) of each archived event, events 1-4 at $FD7A, $FD83, $FD8C, $FD95, written by archive_event ($FFCF). Nothing in this snapshot reads them
Skater ids of the top three of events 1-4, 3 bytes each ($FD9E-$FDA9), written by archive_event ($FFE5). Nothing in this snapshot reads them
Skater id per ranking slot, 8 bytes (0-7 here), swapped with the records by the sort ($F7D2), so after the sort $FDAA-$FDAC name the top three
skater_ids from slot 1 ($FDAB), the sort's neighbour index

Buffer for file $0C, the disk-side ID: goto_event fills it with $FF ($F9A9), the stub loads 3 bytes here, and side_check compares each with wanted_side ($FA6B). Side 1's track 18 sector 18 begins 01 01 01, side 2's 02 02 02 (read from the .g64 images); 01 01 01 here
Second byte of the side ID (compared at $FA6B with X = 1)
Third byte of the side ID (X = 2)
The byte before turn_order, read as $FDB5,x to get the previous turn's skater in POOL JOUST ($FEC4)

A flag only High Jump touches in this snapshot: it flips it on a key edge (CIA 1 port B bit 5, $1A24-$1A3C) and, while it is zero, calls $1A96 with A=1 ($19C7). Kept here so it survives loads; its meaning in game terms is not established
Non-zero in practice (the town): results are not stored and the event ends at PRACTICE AGAIN? ($FE29). File $0B has 0; the town snapshot has 1, so the hub sets it (its code is not in memory here)
Set to $FF by High Jump on a key edge (CIA 1 port B bit 7, $1A1E) to abandon the event; event_done ($FE21) then clears it and comp_flag and goes to the shop

An event has finished. Text screen, sprites unexpanded; quit_flag goes to the shop. In practice: PRACTICE AGAIN? Clear the result slots and move to the next turn; when every skater has played go to show_results. Otherwise fill slot A (and slot B for events 4 and 5; an odd one out gets LESTER in event 4 and goes to show_results in event 5), print NEXT SKATER, pause and replay the event without loading it (reenter_event)

Inside archive_event (STA $FD7A,x). Operand byte ($FD) of LDA $FDAA,y at $FFE2 in archive_event; the auto symbol is from High Jump JSR $FFE4 at $0AEA (the KERNAL GETIN address), code with no caller found

Bytes $FFEF-$FFF9 that nothing references: the last 9 bytes of file $0B ($FFEF-$FFF7) and two bytes after it

NMI vector, $0A3A. Not written by High Jump or by the resident code; it is the same in the town and shop, where $0A3A is an RTI. In High Jump $0A3A is the middle of the IRQ set-up ($0A3A LDA #$0A ... RTS), so an NMI here would not return properly. $03AB in page 3 is the only code in memory that writes it (with $0954)
RESET vector in RAM, $0954 (written with the NMI vector at $03B0). The CPU fetches it only if a reset happens with RAM mapped, which the hardware reset does not do
IRQ vector, set to $0AF0 by High Jump at $0A37/$0A3C (its raster interrupt). entry.vsf, taken before that, holds $11AD
